what.text: linkding is a self-hosted bookmark manager: a small web app where people keep links in their own installation. It aims to be minimal, fast and easy to run from a single Docker container.

users.who: People who run their own installation
jobs: save a link with a title and tags
write notes and mark links as unread
import and export a bookmark file

users.who: Households or teams sharing one instance
jobs: share a bookmark with other users

users.who: Developers and tinkerers building on it
jobs: manage bookmarks through a REST API
add links from a browser extension
subscribe to a feed of bookmarks
configure the server with environment options

parts.name: Web application
parts.role: Serves the bookmark pages, forms and settings screens

parts.name: Bookmark logic
parts.role: Creates, edits, archives, tags and shares bookmarks; kicks off follow-up jobs

parts.name: Search and filtering
parts.role: Turns a search phrase and tag filters into database queries

parts.name: Data model
parts.role: Stores bookmarks, tags, bundles, files and user preferences

parts.name: REST API
parts.role: Lets extensions and third-party apps manage bookmarks

parts.name: Background tasks
parts.role: Fetch metadata, icons, preview images and page snapshots after saving

concepts.name: Bookmark
concepts.meaning: A saved link with title, description, notes, unread and shared flags

concepts.name: Tag
concepts.meaning: A label attached to bookmarks; tags can be renamed, merged and deleted

concepts.name: Asset
concepts.meaning: A file stored with a bookmark, such as a page snapshot or an upload

concepts.name: Bundle
concepts.meaning: A saved search shown as its own bookmark list

concepts.name: Auto-tagging rule
concepts.meaning: A URL pattern that adds fixed tags whenever a bookmark matches

concepts.name: Profile
concepts.meaning: Per-user display, sharing, icon and search preferences

concepts.name: Token
concepts.meaning: A key that lets a person or a feed read bookmarks without the browser login

concepts.name: Search expression
concepts.meaning: A query of words, phrases, tags and combinators used to find bookmarks

features.userAction: Search by words, phrases and tags with and/or/not

features.name: Bulk actions

features.userAction: Share a bookmark with other users or guests

features.userAction: Keep an HTML snapshot or a copy on the Internet Archive

features.userAction: Define URL rules that add tags automatically

features.userAction: Save a search as a named list and reorder lists

features.userAction: Move bookmarks in and out, or drive them from other apps

experienceNotes: Adding a bookmark: the person types the URL, then tags (space separated, no hash), then title and description by hand. Nothing is filled in automatically on this form until saving.

After the URL is entered, the title gets filled in automatically from the page ("Example Domain") and the tag field suggests existing tags matching what is typed; the description stays empty and must be written by hand.

After saving, the person lands back on the bookmark list with the new link at the top. The title stayed the generic page title ("Example Domain") even though it is an article about Prague, so fixing the title means opening Edit afterwards.

Search is by literal words and tags: typing "pasta" and pressing Enter finds "Fresh pasta by hand" by its title. A word that only appears in the meaning of a page, not in its title, tags or description, would not be found.

The main settings page holds one long form with per-user preferences plus admin pieces: auto tagging is a text box where each line maps a URL pattern to fixed tags, and there are switches for bookmark sharing, favicons, preview images and Internet Archive snapshots.

Opening a bookmark's details shows a small panel with its link, archive snapshot link, archived/unread checkboxes, a file upload, its tags and the date added, plus Edit and Delete. There is no place that shows what the page is actually about.

On the add form, the person has to recall the right tags themselves; the field only suggests tags once typing starts. There is no sharing switch on the form, so sharing a new bookmark is a separate step afterwards.

# Product Backlog

Based on Decision_Doc version 1.

## S1 Ask for suggested tags and a one-line description on the save form (priority 1, effort medium)

As a person who saves bookmarks, I want to ask for suggested tags and a one-line description on the add form and keep only the ones I like, so that I type less while staying in control of what gets saved.

**Acceptance criteria**
- With the person's AI switch off, the add form looks and behaves exactly as today and no model call is made.
- With the switch on, pressing the help button on the add form returns at least one suggested tag drawn from the person's own existing tags and a one-sentence description of the page, within the short time limit.
- Every suggestion is shown as a proposal with keep and ignore; ignoring all of them saves the bookmark exactly as typed, and keeping one saves only what was kept.
- When the model is slow, unreachable or returns nonsense, the add form shows no error page, stays usable and saves what the person typed.
- Only the address, page title, description and the person's own tag names are sent for a suggestion; no other user's tags or bookmarks are read.
- The model address, key and model name are read only from the three AI environment variables, and the tests replace the model call with a stub.

**Demo point:** On the add form, type an address, press the help button, see suggested tags from the person's own tags plus one one-sentence description; keep one suggestion and ignore the rest, save, and the bookmark holds exactly what was kept. With the switch off, the form is unchanged.

**Feature_Contract** (changes the software's code; at most 3 attempts, 10 min)

Suggested tags and a one-sentence description on the save form, behind the person's own switch

Should do:
- Add one switch to the person's own preferences, off by default, that turns AI help on for that person
- Show a help button on the add form only when that person's switch is on and the installation-wide switch allows it
- Send only the address, page title, description and the person's own tag names to the model, through the one shared client
- Show at least one suggested tag chosen from the person's own existing tags and one one-sentence description, each as a proposal with keep and ignore
- Leave the form untouched until the person presses keep; save exactly what is left in the form
- Keep the model call inside the save request with a short time limit, and leave the form as it is today when the call fails or times out
- Read the model address, key and model name only from the three AI environment variables, and stub the model call in tests

Should not do:
- Fill tags, titles or descriptions into a saved bookmark without the person pressing keep
- Call the model when the person's switch is off
- Store the suggestions or any page text on the bookmark
- Read or send other users' shared, guest-visible or private bookmarks and tags
- Write a model client of its own; only the shared client talks to the model
- Run the suggestion as background work after saving

Checks run by the Verifier (code, no AI):
- c1: Runs the tests: python manage.py test bookmarks.tests.test_ai_suggestions (at most 600 s)
- c2: In the browser: open /bookmarks/new, then type “https://example.org” into “URL”, then click the button “Suggest tags”, then see the button “Save”, then see “Suggested”
- c3: Reads the data back from the app and expects https://example.org present with archived = false

References: workflow:w1, scope, approach:chosen, acceptance, ui-impact, ai-runtime

## S2 One switch that turns AI help off for the whole installation (priority 2, effort small)

As an instance administrator, I want one switch that turns AI help off for the whole installation, so that I can be sure no bookmark data leaves my server even if a person switched the help on.

**Acceptance criteria**
- An administrator setting exists that switches AI help off for the whole installation, and it is on (help allowed) unless the administrator changes it.
- The administrator setting is checked before the person's own switch on every request: when it is off, the help button is gone on the add form for everyone and no model call is made, even for a person whose own switch is on.
- When it is switched back on, people whose own switch is on get the help button again.
- Nothing else on the settings screens changes, and the existing settings tests keep passing.

**Demo point:** As administrator, turn the installation-wide AI switch off, then open the add form as a person who had switched help on: the help button is gone and nothing is sent. Switch it back on and the button returns.

**Feature_Contract** (changes the software's code; at most 3 attempts, 10 min)

An installation-wide switch that turns all AI help off, next to the existing administrator settings

Should do:
- Add one administrator setting that switches AI help off for the whole installation, defaulting to allowed
- Honour the administrator setting before the person's own switch: when it is off, no AI help is shown and no model call is made
- Make the help button disappear again as soon as the administrator switches it off, and return when switched back on
- Show the setting plainly on the administrator settings screen with a short explanation of what it turns off

Should not do:
- Turn AI help on for anyone; the person's own switch stays off by default
- Send any data to the model while the administrator has it switched off
- Change the person's own switch or any other setting on the settings screens
- Duplicate the enable logic in each screen instead of checking the administrator setting in one place
- Add a second model client or any second place that talks to the model

Checks run by the Verifier (code, no AI):
- c4: Runs the tests: python manage.py test bookmarks.tests.test_ai_suggestions (at most 600 s)

References: scope, workflow:w1, risks, ai-runtime

# Requirements

Based on Decision_Doc version 1.

This lists every acceptance criterion of the two stories as a numbered requirement, so a developer can check each one off. Each item says which story it belongs to and how it is accepted: by a browser demonstration the Judge can watch, by an automated test that replaces the model call with a stub, or by checking the saved bookmark. The requirements cover the save-form help for the person who switched it on, and the installation-wide switch the administrator controls.

## R1 (story S1)
With the person's AI switch off, the add form looks and behaves exactly as it does today and no model call is made.

Acceptance:
- Browser: with the switch off, open the add form, type an address and save; no help button appears and the bookmark saves as typed
- Test: with the switch off, the model stub is never called

## R2 (story S1)
With the switch on, pressing the help button on the add form returns at least one suggested tag drawn from the person's own existing tags and a one-sentence description of the page, within the short time limit.

Acceptance:
- Browser: open the add form, type an address, press the help button, see a suggestion area labelled as suggested, a tag from the person's own tags and a one-sentence description
- Test: with the switch on and a stubbed model answer, the response contains at least one tag that exists in the person's own tag list

## R3 (story S1)
Every suggestion is shown as a proposal with keep and ignore; ignoring all of them saves the bookmark exactly as typed, and keeping one saves only what was kept.

Acceptance:
- Browser: ask for suggestions, ignore all of them, save, and the bookmark holds exactly the tags, title and description that were typed
- Browser: ask for suggestions, keep one tag and ignore the rest, save, and the bookmark holds only the kept tag
- Test: saving after ignoring every suggestion stores no suggested value

## R4 (story S1)
When the model is slow, unreachable or returns nonsense, the add form shows no error page, stays usable and saves what the person typed.

# Technical Architecture

Based on Decision_Doc version 1.

Two switches and one server-side suggestion call. A new per-person boolean (off by default) and a new installation-wide boolean (allowed by default) go on the two models that already hold such switches, edited through the settings page that already renders both forms — the profile form for everyone and the global form for superusers only. One new service module holds the only model call and the single enable check (installation first, person second). A read-only action on the existing bookmark API viewset, next to the page-metadata lookup the add form already calls, answers with tags drawn from the person's own tag names plus one one-sentence description. The add form gets one button and a small proposal panel; fields are written only when the person presses keep. Nothing is stored on boo…

## Affected parts of the existing software

### Person's preferences (bookmarks/models.py, bookmarks/forms.py)
One more boolean beside the existing per-person switches, off by default, listed in the profile form with the existing checkbox widget so the settings page renders it without new plumbing.

Sources (checked by Studio code):
- bookmarks/models.py:441 — found: `enable_favicons = models.BooleanField(default=False, null=False)`
- bookmarks/forms.py:308 — found: `class UserProfileForm(forms.ModelForm):`
- bookmarks/forms.py:322 — found: `"enable_favicons",`

### Installation-wide settings (bookmarks/models.py, bookmarks/forms.py)
One more boolean on the existing single global-settings row, defaulting to allowed, added to the global settings form.

Sources (checked by Studio code):
- bookmarks/models.py:558 — found: `enable_link_prefetch = models.BooleanField(default=False, null=False)`
- bookmarks/forms.py:376 — found: `fields = ["landing_page", "guest_profile_user", "enable_link_prefetch"]`

### Settings screen (bookmarks/templates/settings/general.html, bookmarks/views/settings.py)
The administrator switch is NOT a separate screen: the same settings page already renders the global settings form, but only for superusers. The new checkbox is added to that existing section, next to the prefetch switch; no new view, url or form class.

Sources (checked by Studio code):
- bookmarks/views/settings.py:46 — found: `global_settings_form = GlobalSettingsForm(instance=GlobalSettings.get())`
- bookmarks/templates/settings/general.html:245 — found: `{% if global_settings_form %}`
- bookmarks/templates/settings/general.html:270 — found: `{% formfield global_settings_form.enable_link_prefetch label="Enable prefetching links on hover" has_help=True %}`
- bookmarks/templates/settings/general.html:185 — found: `{% formfield form.enable_sharing label="Enable bookmark sharing" has_help=True %}`

### Model call and enable check (bookmarks/services/ai_suggestions.py, new)
The only module that talks to the model, through the Studio-provided client library (no env reading of its own, no address, key or model name in code). It also holds is_enabled(), the one place that reads the installation switch first and the person's switch second.

Sources (checked by Studio code):
- bookmarks/middlewares.py:35 — found: `request.global_settings = global_settings`
- bookmarks/models.py:21 — found: `class Tag(models.Model):`

### Suggestion endpoint (bookmarks/api/routes.py)
One read-only action on the existing bookmark viewset, right beside the metadata lookup the add form already calls. It inherits session login, the default authenticated permission class and the api-root reverse the form script already uses; it answers 403 before any model call when either switch is off.

Sources (checked by Studio code):
- bookmarks/api/routes.py:105 — found: `def check(self, request: HttpRequest):`
- bookmarks/settings/base.py:150 — found: `"DEFAULT_PERMISSION_CLASSES": ["rest_framework.permissions.IsAuthenticated"],`
- bookmarks/templates/bookmarks/form.html:136 — found: `const requestUrl = `{% url 'linkding:api-root' %}bookmarks/check?url=${websiteUrl}`;`

### Add form (bookmarks/templates/bookmarks/form.html, bookmarks/views/bookmarks.py)
A button and a proposal panel appear only when the new view context flag is true; the existing inline script gets one fetch and keep/ignore handlers that write into the inputs only on keep, using the same value-changed event the metadata prefill already uses so the tag autocomplete picks the value up. The save path is untouched.

Sources (checked by Studio code):
- bookmarks/templates/bookmarks/form.html:66 — found: `{% if request.user_profile.enable_sharing %}`
- bookmarks/templates/bookmarks/form.html:31 — found: `<button id="refresh-button" class="btn btn-link suffix-button" type="button">Refresh from website</button>`
- bookmarks/templates/bookmarks/form.html:118 — found: `input.dispatchEvent(new Event('value-changed'));`
- bookmarks/templates/bookmarks/form.html:152 — found: `// Workaround: tag input will be replaced by tag autocomplete, so`

### Tests (bookmarks/tests/test_ai_suggestions.py, new)
One new Django test module covering both switches, the endpoint with a stubbed model call, and the rendered add form with the switches on and off, following the existing view-test style.

Sources (checked by Studio code):
- bookmarks/tests/test_bookmark_new_view.py:192 — found: `def test_should_respect_share_profile_setting(self):`

## New components
- **bookmarks/services/ai_suggestions.py**: The only module that calls the model (through the Studio-provided client) for suggestions, and the one enable check used by the endpoint and the view. (connects to graftlab_ai (Studio-provided client), bookmarks.models.UserProfile, bookmarks.models.GlobalSettings, bookmarks.models.Tag, bookmarks.api.routes.BookmarkViewSet, bookmarks.views.bookmarks.new)
- **GET /api/bookmarks/suggest/ (read-only action on the existing bookmark viewset)**: Answers one request with suggested tags drawn from the person's own tag names and one one-sentence description; 403 when either switch is off; empty lists instead of an error when the model fails. (connects to bookmarks/services/ai_suggestions.py, bookmarks/templates/bookmarks/form.html)
- **Suggestion panel on the add form**: Shows the suggestions as proposals with keep and ignore and writes into the title, tag and description inputs only when the person presses keep. (connects to bookmarks/templates/bookmarks/form.html)
- **bookmarks/tests/test_ai_suggestions.py**: The test module the acceptance checks run. (connects to bookmarks/services/ai_suggestions.py, bookmarks/api/routes.py, bookmarks/views/bookmarks.py, bookmarks/templates/bookmarks/form.html)

## Data and configuration changes
- New field UserProfile.enable_ai_suggestions, boolean, default off, migration 0043 (depends on 0042_userprofile_custom_css_hash); existing rows keep working on the default.
- New field GlobalSettings.enable_ai_suggestions, boolean, default allowed, migration 0044; the single row is still read through GlobalSettings.get().
- No change to Bookmark: no suggestion, description or page text is stored.

## Technical decisions

### Decision 1: The suggestion call runs inside the request the person triggers with the button, with a 10 second limit and an empty fallback.
**Why:** The background worker does not run in the changed app, so anything the person must see on the form has to be computed while they wait.

**Rejected alternatives:**
- Queue the suggestion as follow-up work after saving
- Compute suggestions for every save whether or not the person asked

### Decision 2: Both switches are stored fields on existing models (profile and global settings), not environment variables.
**Why:** The decision asks for a per-person switch and an installation-wide switch an administrator can flip; both models already carry such switches.

**Rejected alternatives:**
- A Django/environment setting for the installation switch
- A separate settings model for one flag

### Decision 3: The administrator switch goes into the existing global settings section of the same settings page, which the view already renders for superusers only.
**Why:** Reading the code corrects the assumption that admin settings live on their own screen: the same page loads the global form when the user is a superuser.

**Rejected alternatives:**
- A new administrator settings page
- A Django admin entry for the switch

### Decision 4: One enable check lives in the service module and is read first by the endpoint (403 before the model call) and once in the add-form view, which passes a single context flag to the template.
**Why:** Keeps the off state honest in one place instead of repeating the condition in the template, the script and the endpoint.

**Rejected alternatives:**
- Checking either switch separately in the endpoint and in the template condition
- A template condition on the request attributes

### Decision 5: Suggestions are answered by a read-only action on the existing bookmark API viewset, beside the metadata lookup.
**Why:** The add form already calls that same viewset through the api-root reverse, so it inherits session login, the authenticated permission class and the request plumbing with no new url or auth code.

**Rejected alternatives:**
- A new standalone view with its own url and auth handling
- A second API router and viewset

### Decision 6: The model only chooses from tag names the person already has (up to 100 sent); unknown names are dropped and the answer is capped at a few tags and one sentence.
**Why:** The story says suggestions come from the person's own tags, and dropping unknown names keeps the list short and free of surprises.

**Rejected alternatives:**
- Letting the model invent new tag names
- Sending other users' tag names as the candidate list

## Run environment (proposed by the Planner from the software's own files; not a Studio recipe)

Build:
- `python manage.py migrate`
- `python manage.py collectstatic --no-input`

Start:
- `python manage.py runserver --insecure 0.0.0.0:8000`

App port 8000, health path `/health`.

- Makefile:3 — found: `BIND ?= 127.0.0.1:8000`
- bookmarks/urls.py:111 — found: `path("health", health_view, name="health"),`

# Feature Breakdown

Based on Decision_Doc version 1.

Each Feature is built on its own branch, reviewed, verified by its tests and merged into main before the next one starts.

## F1 AI switch in the person's own preferences (story S1, size M)

Adds one per-person preference that turns AI help on, off by default, saved through the settings page that already exists, with the migration that adds the field.

**Scope**
- Modules: bookmarks
- Files expected to change: `bookmarks/models.py`, `bookmarks/forms.py`, `bookmarks/templates/settings/general.html`, `bookmarks/migrations/0043_userprofile_enable_ai_suggestions.py`
- Must not touch: bookmarks/api/routes.py; bookmarks/templates/bookmarks/form.html; bookmarks/views/bookmarks.py; the search implementation; the auto-tagging rules; the other settings on the settings page

**Interfaces**
- UserProfile.enable_ai_suggestions: BooleanField(default=False, null=False)
- "enable_ai_suggestions" added to UserProfileForm.Meta.fields and to Meta.widgets as FormCheckbox
- Settings page checkbox labelled "Enable AI suggestions" with a one-line help note, inside the existing profile form (saved by the existing profile Save button)
- Migration bookmarks/migrations/0043_userprofile_enable_ai_suggestions.py, depends on 0042_userprofile_custom_css_hash

**Detail design**
- Uses no model.
- Data changes: New field UserProfile.enable_ai_suggestions, boolean, default off, plus its own migration file
- Visible texts: "Enable AI suggestions", "Save"

**Tests**
- Files: `bookmarks/tests/test_ai_suggestions.py`
- Command: `python manage.py test bookmarks.tests.test_ai_suggestions`

**Serves acceptance checks:** c1

**Quality (LLM assessment, not a guarantee):** vertical slice ✓ · independent ✓ · testable ✓ · small ✓ · in scope ✓ — Ships the field, its migration and the visible settings checkbox together; four changed files plus the test module, inside M.

**Feasibility:** fits yes, size right; missing: Missing the migration as its own delivered file (models.py change alone breaks the app); should name the settings form class in bookmarks/forms.py and confirm profile fields are edited via that form. Test command assumes a test file is created in F1.

## F2 One installation-wide switch for AI help (story S2, size M)

Adds the administrator's switch, allowed by default, on the existing global settings section, plus the single enable check that reads it before the person's own switch.

**Scope**
- Modules: bookmarks
- Files expected to change: `bookmarks/models.py`, `bookmarks/forms.py`, `bookmarks/templates/settings/general.html`, `bookmarks/services/ai_suggestions.py`, `bookmarks/migrations/0044_globalsettings_enable_ai_suggestions.py`
- Must not touch: the person's own switch and its default; the other settings on the settings page; the import and export sections; the landing page and guest profile settings

**Interfaces**
- GlobalSettings.enable_ai_suggestions: BooleanField(default=True, null=False), meaning help is allowed
- "enable_ai_suggestions" added to GlobalSettingsForm.Meta.fields and to Meta.widgets as FormCheckbox
- Settings page checkbox labelled "Allow AI suggestions" in the existing global settings section, which the view renders for superusers only
- bookmarks.services.ai_suggestions.is_enabled(profile) -> bool: reads GlobalSettings.get() first, then profile.enable_ai_suggestions
- Migration bookmarks/migrations/0044_globalsettings_enable_ai_suggestions.py

**Detail design**
- Uses no model.
- Data changes: New field GlobalSettings.enable_ai_suggestions, boolean, default allowed, plus its own migration file
- Visible texts: "Allow AI suggestions", "Save", "Global settings"

**Tests**
- Files: `bookmarks/tests/test_ai_suggestions.py`
- Command: `python manage.py test bookmarks.tests.test_ai_suggestions`

**After:** F1

**Serves acceptance checks:** c4

**Quality (LLM assessment, not a guarantee):** vertical slice ✓ · independent ✓ · testable ✓ · small ✓ · in scope ✓ — Corrects the assumption that admin settings need their own screen: the same page already renders the global form for superusers. Depends on F1 and on the ordering F1, F2, F3, F4.

**Feasibility:** fits doubt, size right; missing: Admin-wide settings likely live in GlobalSettings edited via an admin-only form/screen, not the per-user general settings page — mixing both in one template is wrong. Needs the chosen storage named and the single helper's signature. Also depends on F1's migration; ordering unstated.

## F3 Suggestion answer through the shared AI client (story S1, size M)

The one module that talks to the model plus the read-only endpoint the add form calls, answering with tags from the person's own tag names and one one-sentence description, and refusing before any model call when a switch is off.

**Scope**
- Modules: bookmarks
- Files expected to change: `bookmarks/services/ai_suggestions.py`, `bookmarks/api/routes.py`
- Must not touch: the existing page-metadata lookup behaviour; the bookmark create and update services; the search query code; the auto-tagging matcher; any second model client

**Interfaces**
- GET /api/bookmarks/suggest/?url=...&title=...&description=... -> 200 {"suggested_tags": ["travel"], "description": "A short article about Prague."} (empty lists on failure)
- 403 with no model call when is_enabled(profile) is false
- bookmarks.services.ai_suggestions.suggest_for_request(user, url, title, description) -> dict with suggested_tags and description, empty on failure/timeout
- Candidate tags: Tag.objects.filter(owner=user) names, at most 100 sent
- Model access only through the Studio-provided graftlab_ai client, configured by GL_AI_BASE_URL, GL_AI_API_KEY and GL_AI_MODEL; tests patch the client call

**Detail design**
- Model call 1: Suggest a few tags chosen from the person's own tag names and one one-sentence description of the page behind the address
  - Input: the address, the title and the description typed in the form, plus at most 100 tag names the person already has; nothing from other users and no page text
  - Answer shape: `{"tags": ["prague", "travel"], "description": "A travel article about Prague."}`
  - On failure: 10 second limit, no retry, log the error and answer with empty lists so the form stays exactly as it is; non-JSON answers, unknown tag names and answers longer than the caps are dropped or shortened to empty
- On errors: No error text and no error page; a failed, slow or nonsensical call answers 200 with empty lists so nothing appears on the form.

**Tests**
- Files: `bookmarks/tests/test_ai_suggestions.py`
- Command: `python manage.py test bookmarks.tests.test_ai_suggestions`

**After:** F1, F2

**Serves acceptance checks:** c1

**Quality (LLM assessment, not a guarantee):** vertical slice ✓ · independent ✓ · testable ✓ · small ✓ · in scope ✓ — Two files: the service module and one action next to the existing metadata lookup, which the add form already calls. The client is provided, so no address, key or model name is written in code.

**Feasibility:** fits doubt, size questioned; missing: Needs the graftlab_ai client wiring plus env-var reading plus the endpoint plus the shared enable check — larger than M. Adding a route in bookmarks/api/routes.py is the REST API surface, not the add form's own JSON endpoint; the add form returns an HTML page after POST, so the right attach point is unclear. Missing answer shape, timeout value, and per-user tag-only input.

## F4 Help button and proposals on the add form (story S1, size S)

Shows the button and the proposal panel on the add form only when AI help is enabled, and writes into the fields only when the person presses keep.

**Scope**
- Modules: bookmarks
- Files expected to change: `bookmarks/templates/bookmarks/form.html`, `bookmarks/views/bookmarks.py`
- Must not touch: the bookmark save path and form handling in the view (only a context key is added); the existing page-metadata prefill and refresh button; the bookmark details panel; the bookmark list page; the model call itself

**Interfaces**
- New context key in bookmarks/views/bookmarks.py new(): "ai_suggestions_enabled": ai_suggestions.is_enabled(request.user_profile)
- Add form button "Suggest tags" (type=button) rendered only when ai_suggestions_enabled is true
- Script calls GET {api-root}bookmarks/suggest?url=...&title=...&description=... and renders the panel from the JSON answer
- Panel heading "Suggested tags" with a "Keep" and an "Ignore" per tag, and "Suggested description" with "Keep" and "Ignore"
- "Keep" on a tag appends the tag name to the tags input and dispatches a value-changed event so the tag autocomplete picks it up; "Keep" on the description writes the sentence into the description input; "Ignore" only hides that proposal
- The form's Save button keeps its label "Save" and its behaviour

**Detail design**
- Uses no model.
- Visible texts: "Suggest tags", "Suggested tags", "Suggested description", "Keep", "Ignore", "Save"
- On errors: No error text and no error page: when the call fails, times out or answers nothing, the panel does not appear and the form stays usable and saveable.

**Tests**
- Files: `bookmarks/tests/test_ai_suggestions.py`
- Command: `python manage.py test bookmarks.tests.test_ai_suggestions`

**After:** F3

**Serves acceptance checks:** c1, c2, c3

**Quality (LLM assessment, not a guarantee):** vertical slice ✓ · independent ✓ · testable ⚠ · small ✓ · in scope ✓ — Django tests can prove the button and panel are rendered or absent, but the keep/ignore behaviour that writes into the fields is only verified by the browser check.

**Feasibility:** fits doubt, size right; missing: Template-only change cannot make the button call the model or show proposals without JavaScript and a JSON endpoint; no script file named. Also F1/F2 switch must hide it server-side, and the visible texts used by the browser check (Suggest tags, Suggested) must be listed here.

## Acceptance checks refined in the technical design

### Story S1
The test module is the new one F1 adds and F3/F4 extend, run with the project's Django test command. The browser check now switches the person's own help on first in their own preferences, because it is off by default, then asks for suggestions on the add form and finally presses the add form's Save so the readback has a bookmark to find. The texts are the ones the templates render: the settings …

- c1: Runs the tests: python manage.py test bookmarks.tests.test_ai_suggestions (at most 600 s)
- c2: In the browser: open /settings/general, then click the checkbox “Enable AI suggestions”, then click the button “Save”, then open /bookmarks/new, then type “https://example.org” into “URL”, then click the button “Suggest tags”, then see “Suggested”, then see the button “Save”, then click the button “Save”
- c3: Reads the data back from the app and expects https://example.org present with archived = false

### Story S2
Same test module. F2 proves the administrator switch defaults to allowed, is saved through the existing superuser-only global form, and that the single enable check refuses while it is off even when the person's own switch is on; F4's tests in the same module prove the button is then absent from the add form and returns when the switch is back on.

- c4: Runs the tests: python manage.py test bookmarks.tests.test_ai_suggestions (at most 600 s)

## Reviewer's decision

I checked the Planner's design against the code and changed three things. First, the administrator switch does not need a new screen: the settings view already loads the global settings form and the template already renders it when the user is a superuser, so it goes beside the existing prefetch switch. Second, both migrations are now named as delivered files (0043 for the person's field, 0044 for the installation switch), since a model field without its migration breaks the app. Third, the suggestion endpoint is the right attach point after all: the add form already calls the same API viewset through the api-root address for page metadata, and the new action sits beside it, inheriting login and permissions. I also pinned what the call sends (only what is in the form, never the page body),
